topic: Minimum of a quadratic on a closed interval
problem: For 2 <= x <= 8, the function f is defined by f(x) = (x - 1)^2 + 4. What is the minimum value of f on this interval?

bad.why: The vertex (1,4) lies outside 2<=x<=8; clicking it gives the wrong minimum 4.
Evaluating f only at x=2,3,...,8 samples a continuous interval at integers and could miss an interior minimum.

algebraFirst.description: Reads the vertex x=1 from vertex form, argues f is increasing on [2,8] because the vertex lies left of the interval, and computes f(2)=5.

explanationNotes: Explain that the lowest point of the whole parabola (x=1, value 4) is outside 2 <= x <= 8, so on this interval the graph only rises and the minimum is at the left end, f(2)=5. Graphing with the restriction shows exactly the allowed piece; warn that the unrestricted vertex value 4 is a trap.
notes: The vertex (x=1) lies outside the interval, so f is increasing throughout [2,8] and the minimum is at the left endpoint, f(2)=5. Graph f with the domain restriction {2<=x<=8} and read the minimum directly; do not sample only integer x-values, since the domain is continuous.
